data.name: HowToUse
data.value:
BEFORE YOU START - SETUP REQUIRED =================================
Before using Asset Tag Printer, you must: 1. Install POS.NET Framework (Windows Point of Service) 2. Install your POS printer's OPOS driver(s) 3. Add your printer in Windows Settings > Devices
For detailed setup instructions, see README.md which separates: - Part 1: POS.NET Framework Installation - Part 2: Printer Device Driver Installation
Quick setup checklist: □ POS.NET installed (Settings > Apps > search "Point of Service") □ Printer OPOS driver installed from manufacturer □ Printer added in Windows (Settings > Devices > Printers) □ Can print from Notepad to your printer □ Printer diagnostics pass (Ctrl+D in this app)
If you have questions about setup, consult: - README.md (comprehensive guide with POS.NET and device setup) - Installation.txt (supplementary technical details) - Press Ctrl+D (run diagnostics to check your configuration) - Press F1 (help/updates with shortcuts)
================================= Quick start ================================= 1) Click "Load CSV" and select your file. - File must not be empty and contain valid asset data - Success message confirms number of assets loaded 2) Click a row to see the tag preview on the right. 3) Select one or more assets: - Enter grid mode with Ctrl+Tab - Use Space to toggle rows, Arrow keys to navigate - Or use Ctrl+A to select all, then Space to deselect specific ones 4) Click "Print Selected (or All)" to print: - If rows are selected, it prints those rows - Print buttons are disabled until at least one row is selected 5) Or click "Print Preview" to review tags before printing
Pagination - The asset list displays 12 items per page for better performance and usability. - Use "< Previous" and "Next >" buttons to navigate through pages. - Page indicator shows your current position (e.g., "Page 1 of 5"). - When you change filters, pagination resets to page 1. - Pagination buttons are disabled when not applicable (Previous on page 1, Next on last page) - Keyboard focus intelligently switches between pagination buttons based on state - Pagination works well with ETD systems for batch processing large asset lists. - Perfect for handling large CSV files with thousands of items.
Filtering assets - Use the "Category" dropdown to choose a filter type: * Select "None" for no filtering (shows all assets) * Select "Warehouse" to filter by warehouse location * Select "Acquisition Date" to filter by year acquired - When you select a category, a second dropdown "Filter by:" appears - Choose the specific value (warehouse name or year) - The asset list automatically updates to show matching items - This progressive filtering is cleaner and more intuitive than separate dropdowns
Keyboard shortcuts - Ctrl+O: Load CSV - Ctrl+P: Print selected (requires at least one row selected) - Ctrl+Shift+P: Print preview (requires at least one row selected) - Ctrl+D: Diagnostics - F1: Help / Updates - Ctrl+W: Focus Category filter (opens dropdown) - Ctrl+E: Focus Filter by dropdown (opens dropdown) - Tab: Navigate main window controls ONLY (skips data grid) - Ctrl+Tab: Toggle data grid lock mode ON/OFF (title shows [GRID MODE] when locked) - Shift+Tab: Navigate backward through main window controls - Space: Toggle selection of current row (in grid mode), OR open dropdown (in main window) - Enter: Select item and apply filters - Esc: Close dropdown, or exit grid lock mode - Arrow keys: Navigate grid cells when in lock mode (preserves selections)
Grid lock mode - Multi-select workflow - Press Ctrl+Tab to enter grid lock mode (window title shows [GRID MODE]) - Select rows using Space to toggle: * Arrow Down → Space (select row) * Arrow Down → Space (select next row, previous stays selected) * Continue until all needed rows are selected * Space toggles selection ON/OFF for the current row * Arrow keys navigate without clearing selections - Or use these quick shortcuts: * Ctrl+A: Select all rows * Shift+A: Deselect all rows (clear everything) * Space: Toggle current row (works after Ctrl+A to deselect specific ones) - After selecting rows, press Esc to exit grid mode - Then use Ctrl+P to print selected rows - Tip: The workflow is designed for keyboard-only workflow - no mouse needed!
Data grid lock mode details - Press Ctrl+Tab to enter lock mode (window title shows [GRID MODE] indicator) - While locked: Tab/Shift+Tab navigate between cells (↔ columns), arrow keys navigate rows (↑ ↓) - Normal Tab key in main window SKIPS the grid - it's only accessible via Ctrl+Tab - When in grid lock: keyboard navigation is completely isolated to the grid - Press Ctrl+Tab again: Exit lock mode (title returns to normal) - Or press Esc: Exit lock mode - Focus automatically returns to the button you were using before entering grid mode - Grid lock mode requires data to be loaded (at least one row in the grid) - If grid is empty, Ctrl+Tab will have no effect - Print/Preview buttons are disabled until a selection is made - Pagination handles large datasets efficiently (1000+ items) - Success messages confirm how many assets were printed - The app validates CSV before loading - invalid files show clear error messages - Keyboard focus restoration ensures smooth navigation between grid and buttons

data.name: Installation
data.value:
Installation & Setup Requirements
=== IMPORTANT: See README.md for comprehensive setup guide === This file provides supplementary details. For complete POS.NET and printer driver setup, please refer to README.md which separates: - Part 1: POS.NET Framework Installation - Part 2: Printer Device Driver Installation - Supported Printer Models - APD (Advanced Printer Driver) Reference
System Requirements - Windows 7 or later - .NET Framework 4.8 or higher (for .NET Framework builds) - .NET 8 (for .NET 8 builds with Windows support) - USB or network printer connection
======================================== POS.NET Framework (Required) ========================================
What is POS.NET? POS.NET is Microsoft's Point of Service framework providing standardized APIs for POS peripherals (printers, scanners, displays). Essential for hardware communication.
Download & Install POS.NET: 1. Visit Microsoft Download Center or check if included in OPOS driver package 2. Download "Microsoft Point of Service" or check OPOS driver package (may be included) 3. Run installer and complete setup (default settings recommended) 4. Verify installation: Settings > Apps > Search for "Point of Service" 5. Check directory: C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Point Of Service\Configuration\ 6. Restart computer if prompted
======================================== Printer Device Setup (Required) ========================================
OPOS and APD Driver Overview Asset Tag Printer uses two driver components:
1) OPOS (Open POS) Drivers v1.14+ - Primary interface for POS printer communication - Required for all supported printers - Handles USB and network connections - Provides standardized printing commands across printer brands - Download from your printer manufacturer's website
2) APD (Advanced Printer Driver) Documentation - Contains printer-specific capabilities and settings - Defines supported fonts, paper sizes, DPI, and code pages - Includes label positioning, margin, and alignment options - Specifies thermal vs inkjet printing modes (if supported) - Essential for optimizing print layout and formatting - APD typically available on manufacturer support pages alongside OPOS driver
Installation Steps (Quick Reference) For detailed instructions, see README.md Part 2:
1) Download OPOS driver AND APD documentation from manufacturer 2) Install USB/network drivers if needed for your connection type 3) Run OPOS driver installer and complete setup 4) Add printer via Settings > Devices > Printers & scanners 5) Verify printer appears in device list 6) Test printing from Notepad 7) Consult APD documentation for font, paper width, and DPI settings 8) Use Print Style Editor to configure label layout
Font & Text Styling - Application supports TrueType fonts installed on your system - Font availability depends on your Windows installation - Some fonts may not render correctly on all POS printers due to hardware limitations - Test your font choices with the Print Preview feature before bulk printing - Refer to your printer's APD documentation for supported font formats - Monospace fonts (Courier, Consolas) typically render best on thermal POS printers - Check APD for pitch and point-size limitations on your specific printer model
Print Style & Layout Configuration - Use the Print Style Editor (Ctrl+Shift+E) to configure: * Text alignment and positioning * Font families and sizes * Line spacing and margins * Label dimensions - Save custom styles for reuse - Printer-specific paper/label widths affect layout rendering - Consult your printer's APD (Advanced Printer Driver) documentation for: * Supported paper sizes and widths * Label positioning options * DPI and resolution settings * Sample command sets and examples
APD-Specific Configuration When configuring the Print Style Editor: - Consult APD for exact paper width (58mm, 80mm, or custom) - Verify fonts listed in APD match those used in your labels - Check APD DPI setting to ensure proper resolution (typically 180 or 203 DPI for thermal) - Reference APD for margin and positioning recommendations - Some printers have APD-documented limits on text per line; check before designing labels - APD often includes sample code or command sets; useful for troubleshooting
Troubleshooting See README.md for comprehensive troubleshooting guide, including: - POS Configuration not found errors - Printer not found in Windows - Print job failures - Font rendering issues - Barcode printing issues
Diagnostics Use Ctrl+D in Asset Tag Printer to run system diagnostics: - Lists available POS printers - Explains configuration issues - Provides setup guidance - Verifies POS.NET installation
Support Resources - Check README.md for complete setup and troubleshooting - Epson: https://pos.epson.com/ or https://epson.com/Support/Point-of-Sale/Thermal-Printers/Epson-TM-T88V-Series/s/SPT_C31CA85011 - Use Ctrl+D for application diagnostics - Press F1 for in-app help

Update log
Latest Version (1.4) - DOCUMENTATION: Added comprehensive README.md with separate sections for: * Part 1: POS.NET Framework Installation (Microsoft Point of Service setup) * Part 2: Printer Device Driver Installation (OPOS & printer-specific drivers) * Supported printer models (Epson TM, Star Micronics, Zebra) * APD (Advanced Printer Driver) documentation reference guide * Troubleshooting guide for setup and printing issues - DOCUMENTATION: Updated Installation.txt to reference README and condensed for clarity - DOCUMENTATION: Updated HowToUse.txt with setup requirements checklist - CSV VALIDATION: Simplified column validation - now validates by column index only * No longer checks column header names (coordinator preference) * Validates minimum 4 required columns: Id, Ref, Label, Barcode * Collects ALL errors and displays them together (not one at a time) * Read entire CSV before reporting errors - CSV VALIDATION: Per-row validation for better error reporting * Each row validated individually with row number in error message * Ref, Label, Barcode must NOT be empty (strict required fields) * Warehouse can be empty (location field, optional) * AcquisitionDate can be empty OR must be valid date format
Version 1.3 - CODE QUALITY: Comprehensive code cleanup across all source files * Added meaningful XML documentation (/// <summary>) to all public and key private methods * Improved documentation for Asset, CsvService, PrinterService, TagLayoutFormatter classes * Enhanced form classes (HelpUpdatesForm, PrintPreviewForm, PrintStyleEditorForm) with clear summaries * Replaced redundant inline comments with concise, meaningful documentation * Organized helper methods with clear section headers in ProcessCmdKey method * Improved method organization in MainForm keyboard handlers for better readability - DOCUMENTATION: Cleaner, more professional codebase ready for maintenance and future development - CODE MAINTENANCE: Single source of truth for method purposes - easy to understand for new developers - TESTING: All functionality preserved - no behavioral changes, pure code quality improvements
Version 1.2 - ROBUSTNESS: Button state management - Print/Preview buttons disabled until rows selected - ROBUSTNESS: CSV validation - empty files, missing data, invalid formats now show clear errors - ROBUSTNESS: Selection validation - prevents accidental printing with no selection - ROBUSTNESS: Success feedback - confirms number of assets printed/previewed - Enhanced Grid Lock Mode: Ctrl+Tab now correctly toggles grid mode ON/OFF - Smart Keyword Navigation: Focus intelligently switches between pagination buttons * On Last Page: Next button disabled, focus moves to Previous * On First Page: Previous button disabled, focus moves to Next * Preserves focus position between grid mode and main window - Multi-select Workflow: * Space now toggles row selection consistently without auto-navigation * Arrow keys navigate while preserving all selections * Ctrl+A selects all rows, then Space to deselect specific ones * Shift+A clears all selections - Grid Lock Mode ([GRID MODE] display): * Proper enter/exit with Ctrl+Tab and Esc * Focus restoration to previous button when exiting * Manual cell navigation without auto-select behavior * Fully isolated keyboard navigation for data grid - Keyboard accessibility fully tested and refined for power users - Acquisition date format: YYYY/MM display (e.g., "2024/03" for March 2024)
Version 1.1 - Version label now displays correctly (fixed corrupted version string) - Enhanced keyboard navigation for Category dropdown: * Ctrl+W: Focus and open Category filter * Space: Open dropdown when focused * Enter: Select and apply filters * Escape: Close dropdown - Enhanced keyboard navigation for Filter by dropdown: * Ctrl+E: Focus and open Filter dropdown * Tab: Jump from Category to Filter dropdown (auto-opens) * Space: Open dropdown when focused * Enter: Select and apply filters * Escape: Close dropdown - Main form starts with empty grid (no auto-load on startup) - Users must click "Load CSV" to populate the asset list - Help text now loaded from external .txt files (cached at startup) - Pagination system: Displays 12 items per page for large asset lists - Page navigation with Previous/Next buttons and page indicator - Pagination resets to page 1 when filters change - Optimized for ETD (Electronic Tag Display) systems and batch processing - Pagination works well with large CSV files (1000+ items) - Removed load limit feature in favor of intuitive pagination - UI Refactoring: Replaced separate Warehouse dropdown with unified Category-based filtering - Progressive filter: Second "Filter by" dropdown appears/updates based on selected category - Cleaner, less redundant UI that's more intuitive for asset filtering
Previous Updates - CSV parsing now supports quoted fields (commas inside text no longer shift columns). - Warehouse filter now runs before load-limit (limit no longer gate-keeps matching rows). - Enter key now applies Warehouse/Limit filters for keyboard users. - Enter key now toggles the Limit checkbox when focused (M1-like behavior). - Warehouse dropdown now supports filtering rows where warehouse is blank. - POS/Windows printing support and preview. - Preview and printing share the same line layout builder (so they match). - Multi-row selection enabled for printing (select multiple rows to print in order). - Optional CSV load limit (limit to first N rows for large files). - Warehouse filter (dropdown based on "Default warehouse" column when present). - Help / Updates window with usage notes and update log.
